item.title: LXC and Linux System Containers
item.description:
LXC is a userspace interface for Linux containment features. It combines the liblxc library, command-line tools, and distribution templates to create system containers: isolated Linux userspaces that share the host’s kernel.

An LXC container can boot an init system, run several services, maintain persistent package state, and expose virtual network interfaces. The operating model therefore resembles a lightweight Linux machine more than an OCI application container. LXC remains a container runtime, however, because it does not boot a guest kernel or emulate hardware.

item.title: Installing Slackware in QEMU
item.description:
Slackware retains a direct relationship between its mirror tree, installation media, package series, and text-mode installer. Understanding that structure helps when selecting packages and diagnosing an installation. The examples below install Slackware64 15.0 in a UEFI QEMU virtual machine.

Slackware Resources and Mirror Tree #

The primary project resources are:

  • Slackware Linux for release announcements and project information
  • Slackware Documentation Project for installation and administration documentation
  • Slackware Linux Essentials for the SlackBook
  • Slackware mirrors and the mirror list for release files

item.title: QEMU
item.description:
QEMU provides system emulators, user-mode CPU emulators, and storage tools. A system emulator models a complete machine, including CPUs, memory, firmware, buses, and devices. A user-mode emulator translates a foreign-architecture userspace program and maps its system calls to the host kernel; it does not boot a guest kernel.

System Emulation #

qemu-system-x86_64 creates an x86-64 virtual machine. -m selects guest memory and -smp selects virtual CPUs. Firmware is part of the machine configuration: SeaBIOS provides legacy BIOS on x86, while OVMF provides UEFI firmware. Storage backends and devices are distinct: -blockdev defines a backend and -device attaches a guest controller or device. -drive is a convenient shorthand for common combinations.
